name: SB-12 hero parts
about: Parts manifest read by scripts/blender/parts/build_parts.py (called from build_pipeline_test.py --parts). Every part hangs off a named socket derived from the hull JSON (anchors.py); numbers here are the ones the hull JSON does not carry yet, each with its source. docs/speedboat/parts-log.md has the self-critique per part.

cockpitWell.source: user pick 2026-09-13: cockpit at 55-80 % LOA from the bow (Apache 42, REFERENCES a1); width/sole STYLE-SPEC §2. Grown to contain the helm chain if the JSON seat sits outside it

helm.source: STYLE-SPEC §2 ergonomics chain (eye sheer+0.50, eye 0.90 behind the screen base, dash 5.55-6.00, screen 0.40 tall raked 35°) re-expressed relative to the JSON seat so the helm follows renderOnly.cockpit.seats. Rake read as 35° FROM VERTICAL (55° from horizontal): at 35° from horizontal the top edge lands 0.33 m from the eye and fills the POV, unlike concept 05
helm.ergonomicsSource: pilot-log v2 'Ergonomics blocker' (T192 fold-in): the old hub sat 8 cm BELOW the pan and 0.73 m ahead, forcing a 43° lean with the hands under the face and the wheel out of the cockpit view; the quadrant sat 0.67 m off-centre (24° torso roll + 54° wrist bend). Hub now 0.30 above / 0.50 ahead of the pan (upright racing seat, bent elbows), the shaft running down to the dash face below the gauge cluster; the middle throttle handle 0.40 outboard (natural reach 0.35–0.45), at forearm-rest height (pan + 0.20), 0.40 ahead

outboard.source: Mercury Racing 450R class (REFERENCES d6): 30 in shaft, 26 in minimum centre spacing -> cowl <= 0.6 m wide

seat.source: STYLE-SPEC §2 seat pan 0.62 above the sole (seat.py); the pilot frame's origin is this pan top at the JSON seat station (pilot-log v2)

deckShape.source: USER playtest (§T.192): 'the back and the top of the boat are too flat. a bit of a taper like in our initial reference' (concept 04 / 06b). Render-only: the deck CENTRELINE stays on the proxy deck (checker deck ±2 cm); the deck falls away toward the sheer as a parabola (4.5 cm at 1.23 m half-beam, a 2.4 m offshore deck's usual camber) and the aft deck slopes down to the transom over its last 2.3 m (7 cm); the sheer edge radius grows 15 → 35 mm. Every part that lands on the deck asks anchors.deck_surface_y(x, z)

M_Carbon.looks: cowl paint, lower-unit paint, carbon dash, vents

M_Metal.looks: trim sheet: stainless, aluminium, cast gearcase, props, rams, rubber rub rail, antenna

M_Cockpit.looks: seat vinyl, harness, gauges, tablet, radio, governor, levers, jerry cans, cases, straps, rope

slots.note: ormScale/baseScale downsample the composited map (2×2 box, deterministic) after the bake: exterior roughness/AO holds at half res; GPU texture memory is shared by all 8 boats and the hero hull + pilot still have to fit (browser sync 2026-09-13: 56 MB for this set)

texelDensity.note: tier RATIOS are exact (1 : 2 : 0.5); absolute px/m is what the 2048² atlas fits and is printed per slot. Need: chase cam (7.5 m, 60° vFOV, 1080p) ≈ 125 px/m on screen → exterior ≥ 256; cockpit cam at 0.5–1 m ≈ 700–1400 px/m → cockpit tier carries fine detail in normal/roughness. 'low' = big simple surfaces only seen from outside (rub rail, bracket plates)

budget.note: player LOD0 <= 120k TOTAL (assetContract). Measured split (§T.192): hull ~29.5k + parts ≤ 64k + pilot v2 17.9k ≈ 111k, 9k margin (the old 40k hull line was never used; pilot v2 is 17.9k not 14k). LOD1 hull 4.7k / parts 9.8k / pilot 6.1k; LOD2 hull 0.6k / parts 3k / pilot 2k

nodeGroups.note: `nodes` names the GLB node a part joins at LOD0/1/2. Parts sharing a name are joined into one mesh (one primitive per slot) — the draw budget (assetContract drawBudget). Animated parts keep their own node at LOD0; at LOD1 each outboard folds its prop into `Drive_<id>` (§T.192: every drive steers about ITS OWN swivel tube, extras carried from the outboard), at LOD2 everything is `Parts`. `GaugeGlass` (LOD0 only) is the see-through surface below the sheer that the runtime must draw before the water mask.
